_doc: NPC_AI_SPEC §5.1 / §12 — which intrinsic actions an archetype offers and
which need profile (needs.json) drives it.
`intrinsic` is CONTENT, not code: phase 1 stores the list on the agent and
the debug overlay prints it. The UtilityReasoner (phase 5) is what turns
these ids into scored candidates, alongside affordance-derived actions.
Updated 2026-07-28 (phase 5.3, found missing during the phase-5
validation pass): villager gained flee_to_safety/sleep/gather_resource/
haul_to_deposit (5.6/5.7's own action ids, none of which existed here
before — gather_resource and haul_to_deposit only ever apply once a
villager has a job, gated at candidate-assembly time, not by archetype).
guard's 'flee' renamed to 'flee_to_safety' to match §5.6's real id — it
was never consumed by any live code, confirmed via grep, so this is a
content fix, not a behavior change. guard intentionally did NOT gain
'sleep': defenders keep the OPPOSITE hours to working villagers
(isWatchHours, data/villagers.ts) and are driven separately by
Defenders.tsx, not by this reasoner yet — whether/how a guard rests is
an open question for whenever defender AI actually gets built, not
something to silently assume works the same way as a villager's night.
Updated 2026-08-03: villager gained idle_fidget/notice_player (ambient.ts/
notice.ts) — real ambient-category/social-category content, both scored
so low they only ever win during genuine downtime (see those files' own
headers). New 'court' archetype: ONLY those same two actions, nothing
movement/schedule-related — deliberately narrower than villager so a
court NPC (King Leo, Richard, Storm, the starter farmers — anyone
courtAmbientSync.ts spawns an Agent for) can never wander off post or
flee a raid three regions away, while still reading as alive via the
same fidget/notice content a working villager gets.
Updated 2026-08-10 (Wave 10): villager gained seek_deposit (a stranded
hauler's walk back into haul_to_deposit's own query radius) and
tend_farmplot (the farmer's plant/harvest cycle, which gather_resource
was never shaped to run). Deliberately villager-only: neither belongs to
a court NPC or a guard, who have no sack and no job. NOTE for anyone
reading this list as a manifest — 'wander', 'socialize' and 'idle' have
NO real Action behind them in src/ai/actions and never have;
assembleCandidates silently skips ids with no registered action, so they
are aspirational content, not behaviour. That gap is exactly why a
stranded carrying villager had nothing at all to move them before
seek_deposit existed. ('wander' stopped being aspirational in phase 8 —
see the note two paragraphs down. 'socialize' and 'idle' still are.)
Updated 2026-08-11 (Wave 11, phase 7): villager gained take_cover
(actions/takeCover.ts) — the first combat-category action any archetype
here has ever been offered, and the first thing in the game to react to a
hostile a villager can actually PERCEIVE (phase 6) rather than to the
global raid flag flee_to_safety gates on. guard's own take_cover and
engage_threat ids stop being aspirational in the same pass: both now have
real registered Actions (actions/index.ts). guard is still never spawned by
any live code path — engage_threat's own capability gate is job ==
'defender', which is exactly the job rosterSync.ts excludes from having an
Agent, so it cannot fire for anyone today. That is deliberate and is
argued in full in actions/engageThreat.ts's header; reversing the exclusion
is a migration off Defenders.tsx's shipped, tuned combat AI and needs its
own sign-off, not a quiet config edit here. take_cover is deliberately NOT
given to 'court': that archetype's whole point (below) is that a court NPC
can never leave their post, and a cover point is by definition somewhere
else. companion's follow_leader/assist_leader remain aspirational — this
game has no follower entity for them to be about (see PHASE_STATUS.md's
phase 7 section).
Updated 2026-08-11 (Wave 11, phase 8): 'wander' finally has a real Action
(actions/wander.ts) — and is the ONLY entry in this file that needed no
edit at all to go live, having sat first in villager's list since phase 1.
It carries its own capability gate rather than being handed out per
archetype: it fires only for a tier-D roster villager, i.e. one no renderer
is mounting, because every other agent already has Villagers.tsx's shipped
cascade moving them and a competing MOVE_TO would starve it. That is why
'guard' and 'ambient' can keep listing 'wander' below with no effect —
neither is spawned by any live code path, and the gate would decline them
anyway (it requires a roster job, which only a real villager has).
